Use it in the browser, or install the app

Nothing to install to try Trycord: the web client is the same code the desktop app wraps. The desktop build puts that client in its own window and can point at any instance, including one you run.

Two ways in

Use it in a tab, or install the app

Same client either way. Look around in the browser with nothing to install; install a build when you want Trycord out of the tab.

No install

In the browser

The web client is served by the instance itself. Open it, and you are in: no download, no store, and it always matches the server it came from.

Open the web app

Desktop

The desktop app

A window around the same client, for people who want Trycord off the browser tab. Published builds are attached to GitHub releases.

See releases

How the desktop app works

One client, pointed at any instance

The desktop app is the same client in its own window. Nothing is kept in sync, and a feature that works in the browser works in the window.

It picks a backend at launch

First the --api-url argument, then the bundled backend file. There is no hidden third option and no silent fallback to somewhere you did not choose.

Point it at your instance

Run it with your server's address and it talks to that one and nothing else:

Trycord --api-url=https://chat.example.org

The official instance is a default, not a requirement

The shipped build reaches the official instance out of the box, because most people arrive without a server. Self-hosters replace that with theirs, and the desktop origin must be on the instance's allowed list for API responses to be readable.

Build from source

If there is no build for your platform yet

Each target builds on its own platform. Cross-building from Linux is not reliable for Windows or macOS, so build on the system you are targeting.

cd trycord-desktop
npm install
npm run build:linux      # AppImage
npm run build:win        # NSIS installer and portable exe
npm run build:mac        # dmg

The desktop shell's internals, startup behaviour and update model are documented in docs/desktop.md and docs/launcher.md.

Hosting it yourself

If you run the instance, you decide who gets in.

The documentation covers Docker, manual installs, databases, mail and reverse proxies.
